text:
yara: Support flagged a tenant who saw overlapping billing rows after a stream truncate + reconnect. They see a provisional row and then a separate confirmed row for the same token offsets.

ben: can you paste the trace/session ids and whether this hit a fallback or warm pool?

yara: trace=tr-881 sess=sess-900 region=ap-south. runtime truncated at offset 72, client retried, resume replayed 72 tokens and we get two ledger rows.

zack: pulled minimal logs for sess-900: 
```
2026-05-02T12:11:05Z ingress: accept sess=sess-900 provisional_tokens=230
2026-05-02T12:11:09Z runtime: stream-truncate emitted_prefix=72 reason=client_eof
2026-05-02T12:11:11Z router: resume -> pool-c resume_prefix=72
2026-05-02T12:11:12Z ledger: provisional_insert sess=sess-900 tokens=72 tag=pt-72-xyz
2026-05-02T12:11:14Z ledger: confirm_insert sess=sess-900 tokens=72
```

zack: root cause looks familiar: resumed path writes a fresh provisional and then confirms it; the original provisional from the first connection wasn't tombstoned, so UI shows both.

marta: agreed. two-pronged plan: short-term UI mitigation and long-term provenance/upsert fix.

yara: short-term: console should collapse suspected duplicates to reduce customer confusion. Heuristic: same tenant + same session + overlapping token range > 60% within 72h. Collapsed row shows "suspected-merged provisional+confirm" with a link to raw ledger entries. Default is collapsed.

ben: long-term: introduce a prefix-level prov_key generated at first provisional emission and propagated through handoffs. Ledger provisional rows store prov_key; confirm should be confirm_by_prov_key which upserts the provisional -> confirmed instead of inserting a disjoint confirm row. If prov_key absent, keep current behavior.

zack: implementation notes:
- router: prov_key = base64(hmac(router_salt, req_id || ":" || prefix_start)) generated when first tokens for a prefix are provisionally recorded. Propagate prov_key in the handoff RPC. Feature flag this.
- ledger: add provisional.prov_key column (nullable). Implement confirm_upsert(prov_key, tokens, final=true) which updates existing provisional row to confirmed if prov_key matches, otherwise inserts as today. Add DB index on prov_key with TTL 7d.
- recon: change reconciliation consumer to accept upsert events keyed by prov_key and emit both an audit-diff and an upsert event for backward compatibility.

marta: telemetry: add these metrics so we can monitor rollout impact:
- billing.prov_upsert_attempts (counter)
- billing.duplicate_confirm_detected (counter)
- billing.console_collapses (counter)
Also tag metrics with tenant and region for fast triage.

yara: toolcall corner: we sometimes see toolcall results replayed on resume, which causes overlapping provisional entries for toolcall execution cost. Proposal: extend prov_key to toolcall invocations (prov_key + tool_name) and have tool sidecars dedupe by prov_key+tool. That way toolcall billing is idempotent across retries.

ben: tests: unit tests for ledger.confirm_upsert by prov_key, integration test simulating resume where tombstone race occurs, e2e with toolcall replay asserting single billed invocation. Add chaos tests with packet loss and leader re-election.

zack: console change: merge rows on prov_key if present. For environments without prov_key, keep the heuristic collapse. Provide an "expand to raw" action which shows the original ledger rows with timestamps so audits can verify. Also a hover tooltip explaining the merge semantics.

marta: migration: add prov_key column nullable, backfill rarely (don't backfill across entire DB). Instead, run a reconciliation job that detects obvious overlapping provisional+confirm pairs in the last 7 days and create a synthetic prov_key mapping for those so UI can show them as merged. Annotate affected invoices with a note.

ben: rollout plan: feature-flag prov_key generation in router. Deploy ledger upsert behind a flag. Deploy console read-side that merges when prov_key present plus temporary heuristic collapsing. Canary region for 48h and watch billing.duplicate_confirm_detected. Flip flags region-by-region.

zack: backward compatibility: recon and external consumers may still expect insert_confirm events. Emit an additional audit event when upsert happens: insert_audit + upsert_event to preserve existing consumers until they migrate.

yara: ops-bot: created ticket BILL-2026-412 and configured alert billing.duplicate_confirm_detected > 3/min for any tenant.

ops-bot: created BILL-2026-412 and linked SUP-2026-812.

marta: owners: ben -> router prov_key PR; zack -> ledger upsert + index; yara -> console collapse & expand UX; ben + zack -> recon changes and tests; marta -> telemetry + dashboard.

ben: small proto note: prov_key lifetime should be short (72h), collisions unlikely with HMAC + per-router salt. For multi-prefix sessions we generate prov_key per (req_id, prefix_start). Don't reuse a single per-session key.

zack: DB note: keep prov_key column nullable; confirm_upsert should be a single transactional upsert to avoid races. Add a short circuit: if there is an existing provisional row with same prov_key, update it to confirmed and increment billing.prov_upsert_attempts. If an unexpected conflict occurs, increment billing.prov_key_conflict_errors and fall back to insert and emit an operator alert.

marta: I'll prototype the collapsed UI this week and wire the expand-to-raw link to ledger audit rows. Keep the collapsed behavior feature-flagged for quick rollback.

yara: will open the router PR today and include the handoff proto change + small design doc. zack start ledger PR once router proto is in. ben and marta coordinate recon and console.

ops-bot: support notified and running a one-off reconcile for 72h window to annotate affected customers. Ticket SUP-2026-812 created.

ben: thanks. please paste any more traces here if support surfaces them so we can validate the recon sweep.

marta: thanks all. low-risk gradual rollout, and short-term console collapse should reduce customer confusion immediately.

yara: closing loop: I'll post PR links and the dashboard panel once ready.
